title: Echo Flight incident and the Boeing/SAC report

tellings.quote: The reason I think that it was actually UFO related is there was a Boeing uh uh strategic air command report where they actually looked and they tried to recreate the effect and this is on the Echolight incident.
>> uh Boeing also did a bench test on what's called a logic coupler.
tellings.difference: Names the logic coupler as the part bench-tested and credits James Klotz as a source.
tellings.link_reason: Boeing's bench test of the logic coupler is the Boeing/SAC attempt to recreate the Echo Flight effect that the host describes.

tellings.quote: There's even documentation from Malmstrom's strategic air command itself, saying that they were extremely puzzled around the event and that they had no idea what was going on.
tellings.difference: Stresses that SAC documents say the command was extremely puzzled and had no idea what happened.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell of the 1967 Echo Flight/Malmstrom SAC documentation and Boeing's investigation into the shutdown.

as_told.title: SAC documents show puzzlement and a Boeing investigation

tellings.quote: Importantly, other persons have substantiated Col. Figel's account of a UFO-presence during the Echo Flight incident. The late Robert J. Kaminski, who headed the Boeing Company missile engineering team that investigated the case, says he was told by a Boeing–Air Force liaison that UFOs had indeed been sighted in the vicinity of the flight's launch silos at the time of the missile malfunctions. Kaminski unequivocally states that his team could find no prosaic cause for the failures.

Kaminski further says that the Air Force interrupted his investigation in mid-stream and ordered him not to file a report on the full-flight shutdown—an unprecedented and still-unexplained development.

plain: After ten American nuclear missiles failed at once in Montana in 1967, Boeing, which built them, and Strategic Air Command, the Air Force command in charge of nuclear bombers and missiles, are said to have investigated and found no ordinary cause. That would point to something unexplained behind the shutdown. Michels says on the show that a Boeing and Strategic Air Command report on the Echo Flight incident tried to recreate the effect, and that this is why he thinks it was UFO related. Echo Flight was a group of ten missile silos run from Malmstrom Air Force Base. In another episode Michels says the command's own documents show it was 'extremely puzzled' and had 'no idea what was going on'. A former Air Force officer named Robert Salas, crediting a researcher named James Klotz, adds that Boeing 'did a bench test on what's called a logic coupler', a part of the missile's electronics. The researcher Robert Hastings, in an article published on 12 November 2012, gives the account of the late Robert J. Kaminski, who led Boeing's engineering team on the case. A liaison told Kaminski that UFOs 'had indeed been sighted' near the silos at the time, and Kaminski says 'his team could find no prosaic cause for the failures'. Hastings adds that the Air Force 'interrupted his investigation in mid-stream and ordered him not to file a report' on the full shutdown, so the tellers are Michels, Salas repeating his sources, and Hastings quoting the engineer himself.
